title: Request Hashline Drill: probe UI for correlated spans and timeline filtering
creator: Marta Lopez
description: Design and prototype a compact drill-down panel for the Redwood Console that surfaces correlated requests and their span timelines using a visual \"hashline\" metaphor. The hashline is a horizontal fingerprint representing correlation IDs and distribution of spans across time; hovering/scrubbing the hashline reveals grouped span summaries, cost overlays, and rollout/model variant badges. This ticket focuses on the UX interactions, low-fidelity -> hi-fidelity prototype, developer handoff assets, and a short usability review with Eng and PM. Context: the current Request Inspector shows long waterfall views that are hard to parse when many short spans across services exist. We propose a condensed visual scanline that complements the waterfall while supporting filters (correlation ID, route, model variant, latency bucket) and deep-linking into the full waterfall view.
acceptance_criteria: Hashline overview is visible at top of Request Drill panel showing distribution of spans over request lifetime
Hovering over a hashline segment shows an inline popover with aggregated span metadata (count, top service, p50/p95 latency, token cost estimate)
Scrub/zoom on the hashline updates the expanded waterfall timeline below and retains selected correlation ID highlight
Filters by correlation ID, model variant, and latency bucket work and update both hashline and waterfall in under 200ms in prototype (simulated data)
Rollout/model-variant badges appear on spans and on the hashline when a request touched a canary or fallback path
Accessible keyboard navigation to move between hashline segments and expand popovers; screen-reader labels for core elements
Deep-linkable state (URL) that captures selected time window, correlation ID, and active filters
design_notes: Hashline unit is 25ms visual bins by default with option to auto-scale based on request duration distribution
Color encoding: primary for user service spans, muted for infra/service mesh, accent for model-serving spans; badges for rollout states (green=stable, amber=canary, red=fallback)
Cost overlay: microbadge showing per-segment token estimate computed from token delta heuristic; toggleable to avoid clutter
Popovers should show top-3 spans in that bin and link to the full span detail panel (open in contextual pane)
Performance: precompute aggregated bins on the server for the prototype to keep client rendering cheap; engage Eng for KV cache pre-aggregation API
When span density is high, show micro-sparklines inside hashline segments to indicate variability instead of full bars
Design should fit inside existing Request Inspector layout and respond to narrow widths (minimum 920px for full experience)
Edge case: for air-gapped/private deployments, omit cost overlay by default and surface an admin toggle in Console settings
decisions: Use a horizontal 'hashline' visualization rather than compressing waterfall rows to preserve temporal intuition
Aggregate spans into fixed-size bins for overview then allow precise waterfall zoom for inspection
Badge model variant at span-level so UX reflects rollouts and automatic fallbacks
Expose an explicit 'Show cost' toggle for legal/regulatory-sensitive customers
Prototype interactions implemented in Figma with interactive components; handoff will include CSS token guidance and an accessibility checklist
review_feedback: PM (Priya Patel): prioritize linking rollout badges to the Rollouts console so engineers can jump to the policy that caused fallback
Eng (Diego Morales): pre-aggregated bins OK, but need API contract for correlation-join fields; added dependency ENG-41208
Security (Samira Khan): ensure deep-link tokens do not leak PII; sanitized IDs only
Design (Ethan Shaw): reduce visual noise when both cost overlay and badge anchors are enabled; propose hover-only cost microbadges
Accessibility reviewer (Noah Patel): keyboard focus must follow a logical left-to-right order along the hashline; need ARIA labels for each bin summarizing counts/latency
notes: Next steps: schedule 30-min design review with Eng and PM (week of 2026-03-15), iterate high-fidelity screens based on feedback, and prepare a small implementation spike ticket for backend bin-aggregation API.
Spike ticket suggestion: ENG-41555 (backend bin aggregation + correlation join contract)
If accepted, plan a canary release of hashline as an opt-in Console feature flag for 2 weeks before broad roll-out
